scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “B-semiampleness for compact log-smooth Kähler fibrations” (preprints/B-semiampleness-for-compact-log-smooth-Kahler-fibrations-September-10-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 afad4b593eede2dd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the assumptions above, M is b-semiample. More explicitly, there is a smooth compact Kähler modification µ0 : S → X such that: (a) for every smooth compact Kähler modification ν : S1 → S, MS1 = ν∗ MS in Pic(S1)Q; (b) for some positive integer m, the actual line bundle representing mMS is generated by its global holomorphic sections. The theorem includes a point base and relative dimension zero. No projectivity of f, X, or Y is assumed.
